subject: Private VPC pricing recap & next steps

Subject: Private VPC pricing recap & next steps

Hi Eduardo / Nina / team,

Great to meet you all earlier 

 — thanks for the time. Quick recap and the items we need to lock down to get a formal proposal in front of Procurement: 

Call recap (high level):
- You’re prioritizing a Private VPC deployment (no shared control plane) for production-facing inference workloads.
- Primary goals: predictable unit economics, strict data controls (in-transit + at-rest), and a 24/7 support SLA for peak trading hours.
- Architecture: 2 production clusters (east/us-east + secondary for DR), 1 staging, optional QA environment.

Info we need to finalize pricing:
1) Expected token volumes (avg/day and peak/day or monthly tokens).
2) Target budget / target $ per 1M tokens you’re aiming for.
3) Number of environments you want included (prod/staging/qa/dev).
4) Preferred support tier (Standard — business hours; Enterprise — 24/7 + 4h SLA).

What I can share right now (high level):
- Private/VPC pricing is typically a combination of a platform license + per-environment fee + optional GPU capacity commitments.
- Example packaging (ballpark): base subscription ~$250k/yr + $20\u201330k/yr per additional environment; Enterprise support add-on ~$50k/yr.
- Unit economics: with quantization + caching we typically see per-1M-token costs range widely ($500\u2013$3,000 per 1M) depending on model, batching, and caching. We’ll provide a tailored estimate once we have volumes.

Attachment: Redwood_Private_Pricing_Recap.pdf (summary + example T&Cs).

Next steps / ask: Can you confirm the items above (volumes + target $/1M + environments) by Wednesday so we can produce a two-option proposal (standard vs enterprise support)? Also indicate who from Procurement should be on a follow-up call \u2014 we can schedule 30 minutes.

Thanks \u2014 looking forward to getting this into procurement.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing recap & next steps

Marissa \u2014 thanks for the recap and the pdf. Quick answers from our side and a few clarifying questions: 

1) Volumes: ballpark for initial rollout: ~5M tokens/day average, peak ~8\u201310M/day. That’s roughly ~150M tokens/month initially; we expect growth over 6\u201312 months.
2) Target $/1M tokens: procurement has pushed a target of <= $3,000 per 1M tokens (we understand this is contingent on commitment/quantization).
3) Environments: we definitely want two prod clusters (active/standby), 1 staging, and 1 QA (so 4 environments total).
4) Support: aiming for Enterprise (24/7) given trading hours overlap \u2014 need clarity on what’s included (on-call, response SLA, runbook support).

Questions:
- How does your licensing model handle additional environments? Do we get the first X environments included?
- Is the $/1M estimate delivered as part of the license (platform cost amortized) or separate on a per-token billing line?
- Do you offer committed token discounts (e.g., annual commit or prepaid credits)?

Procurement (procurement@fintechco.com) \u2014 looped in to schedule a short procurement call; who from your side should join?

\u2014Eduardo
CTO, FintechCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing recap & next steps

Thanks Eduardo \u2014 great context, this is exactly what we need. Answers below and a concrete example for your 5M/day profile.

Licensing & environment model (how we typically structure Private/VPC):
- Platform subscription (annual): covers control plane, upgrades, platform software \u2014 baseline ~ $250,000/yr.
- Environments: first 2 environments included (covers prod-active + prod-standby). Additional environments (staging/qa/dev) typically priced ~ $20,000\u201330,000/yr/env depending on resource footprint. For your ask (4 envs total) expect +$40\u2013$60k/yr.
- GPU capacity: we recommend sizing dedicated GPU pool (commit) for predictable throughput; pricing separate based on vGPU counts or node pools.
- Support tiers: Standard (business-hours, ticket SLAs) \u2014 included; Enterprise (24/7 + 4h response + priority escalation + runbook onboarding) \u2014 add-on typically ~$50,000/yr.

Unit economics example (estimates \u2014 final will depend on model & quantization):
- Example profile: 5M tokens/day => ~150M tokens/month (~150 x 1M units).
- If we price at $2,800 per 1M tokens (example with 12-month commit + quantized model + caching), token cost = 150 * $2,800 = $420,000/month.
- If priced at $1,500 per 1M tokens (higher commitment, aggressive batching/caching), token cost = 150 * $1,500 = $225,000/month.
- Note: token unit price is influenced by: model size, average sequence length, cache hit rate, batching, and whether you run on quantized kernels. We’ll run a quick eval to tighten the range.

Packaging options we’ll propose (two options):
A) Standard Enterprise Package: ~$250k base + $50k enterprise support + $50k for 2 extra envs + token billing at $2,800/1M (monthly).
B) Commitment Package: discounted rate with 12-month commit + prepay: ~$250k base + $40k env + $50k support + token billing at $1,500/1M (with 12-month minimum commit).

Attachments: private_pricing_model_estimates.xlsx (worked examples for 5M/day and 20M/day profiles), pricing_sheet_private_vpc_v2.xlsx.

Next steps:
- Procurement: propose a 30-minute procurement call Thursday 10:00\u201310:30 PT \u2014 I’ll invite Ben (SE) and our legal rep if helpful.
- Eduardo / Nina: confirm which packaging you prefer (A vs B) and whether you can do a 12-month commit for material discounts.

Happy to jump on a call and walk through the numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Eduardo \u2014 quick note from SE side with some unit-econ color and options we can run in a short eval: 

1) Unit economics drivers: model family (LlamaX-2/Redwood-Open), sequence length distribution, cache hit rate, and batching footprint. For typical Fintech conversational flows (avg seq len ~120 tokens, 60% cache hit), the realistic per-1M-token operational cost to Redwood is in the low hundreds; customer price is then a markup + license amortization.

2) What we can do to reach your target (~$3k/1M):
- Quantize models (8-bit/4-bit) + compile kernels \u2014 reduces GPU cycles by ~30\u201350%.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for common prompts \u2014 each 10% cache hit reduces token bill proportionally.
- Commit to a 12-month prepaid token bucket \u2014 allows us to offer steep discounts.

3) Concrete offer we can model for the eval:
- 12-month prepaid commit of 1.8B tokens (150M/month x 12) + platform license + enterprise support => we can target ~$2,800/1M.
- If you can increase commit (or accept a slightly larger base license), we can reach ~$1,500/1M as Marissa noted.

4) Next step from SE: we’ll run a short cost-to-serve eval (48\u201372h) using a 2\u20133 day sample of your traffic (anonymized). Please share a 72h sample of token logs (format: timestamp, model, prompt_len, completion_len, cache_hit) \u2014 I can share a small template. This will let us produce a tight $/1M estimate and a recommended commit profile.

I’ll join the procurement call (Thu 10:00 PT). Adding the HubSpot deal link here for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678

Thanks,
